newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP AFTERNOON UPDATE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP AFTERNOON UPDATE.

text.p: ENGINEERS EXAMINING SAFETY OF OTHER THREDBO LODGES
Engineers at Thredbo are continuing to examine the stability of lodges near the site of the landslide that has left 18 people dead.
The final body was removed from the rubble this morning and investigations are getting underway into the causes of the landslide.
Emergency service workers are still operating at the rescue site, removing the remaining debris, especially the huge concrete slabs that entombed many of the victims.
Police chief superintendent, Bruce Johnstone, says a number of lodges surrounding the landslide site remain closed.
Superintendent Johnstone says a decision will be made about the safety and future occupancy of lodges within the exclusion zone, once geo-technical specialists have finished examining them.
GOVT SLAMMED OVER JOBS FIGURES
One of the country's leading industry groups has joined the Opposition in criticising the Federal Government for a lack of strategy on unemployment.
Bureau of Statistics figures released today showed Australia's jobless rate rose last month, with the number of people looking for work again topping the 800,000 mark.
The Australian Business Chamber said the news that unemployment has risen to 8.7 percent is depressing and has called on the Government to aim for higher economic growth.
Opposition leader Kim Beazley said the jobless figures are flat at a level that is completely unacceptable.
He said the government has no ambitions on employment policy and denies the figures are better than when Labor was in power.
Federal Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone said lowering unemployment will be a long task.
But chamber managing director Philip Holt said Treasurer Peter Costello's re-affirmation of a 3.75 percent growth target will not help reduce unemployment levels.
"The plain fact is to make any kinds of significant inroads into unemployment we need growth much higher than that," Mr Holt said.
"We need it in excess of four and apporaching five percent.
"Everybody's been frightened of growth at that level saying that Australia can't sustain it.
"We simply have to find the means by which we do."
AMP Investments economist Shane Oliver described today's figures as disappointing and said there was "still no clear signs of any upturn".
Senator Vanstone remains confident employment will rise and unemployment will fall within a year.
"And I just don't think it's appropriate at the release of monthly figures to be either jumping up and down or bursting into bitter depression," she said.
"It's a long task ahead to eat into the unemployment Australia's been left with by Labor's mismanagement."
Meanwhile, the Australian Business Chamber said today's figures clearly indicate another cut in interest rates is warranted.
CALL FOR SPECIAL SES VOLUNTEERS FUND
The New South Wales Government will be asked to protect the incomes of hundreds of State Emergency Service volunteers who have spent the past week at Thredbo.
The Services' Executive Director wants a special fund established so his volunteers are not left out of pocket.
The familiar orange overalled SES volunteers are not paid for their time, yet hundreds have played a key role in the Thredbo operation.
The New South Wales Labor Council's Michael Costa says special leave should be introduced to force employers to recognise the community work of SES volunteers.
But SES Executive Director Horrie Howard says another possibility is a special fund for workers returning to find their pay docked for a week's absence.
TOBACCO WHOLESALERS SUSPEND SALES OF CIGARETTES
Three other major tobacco wholesalers have joined W.D. & H.O. Wills in suspending sales of cigarettes, cigars and tobacco.
Tobacco Retailers Association spokesman, Bob Stanton, says Phillip Morris, Rothmans and Foodland are the latest wholesalers to close their books to orders from retailers.
He says the wholesalers will review their positons on Monday when effects of the shift to the Commonwealth collecting State fees on tobacco are, hopefully, more clear.
Mr Stanton believes most retailers will run out of stocks of most popular tobacco products over the weekend, and it is unclear if there will be any deliveries from wholesalers next week.

"The tax collected under the new system will be $500 million in excess of what the States collected collectively. Now, the Federal Government has agreed that that will be refunded to manufacturers, but nobody knows on what basis, and to whom and how and when or why," Mr Stanton said.
SHIP FIRE VICTIM TAKEN TO HOSPITAL
A crew member on a Taiwanese coal ship which caught fire off the southern New South Wales coast has been transferred to Wollongong Hospital with severe burns.
The man was treated by ambulance officers on the ship, five kilometres off the coast, before being transported by the Coastal Patrol to Port Kembla.
The Wollongong Fire Control Supervisor, Rod Nicholls, said fire brigade officers on board the ship had located the scene of the fire with thermal imaging equipment.
But he said they had not been able to assess the extent of the blaze, believed to have started in the ship's sleeping quarters.
CONCERN ABOUT TELEVISION PROGRAMMES REMAINS STEADY

One in five Australians is concerned about the style and content of television programs, according to an official survey. Figures released in the Australian Broadcasting Authority's annual survey show about 20 per cent of the population is still unhappy with Australian television.
The figures, for 1996, are similar to those in the 1995 survey.
The 1996 survey, titled Views on Viewing, involved face-to-face interviews with more than 1,000 people over the age of 14.
Of those surveyed, one in five said they had seen something on television in the previous week which they disliked or which concerned them.
The portrayal of sex and nudity remained the number one complaint, followed by news and current affairs, with advertising and violence closely behind.
The figures are only slightly up from last year's, with concern over sex and nudity showing the most significant increase.
